# Running PocketOne

PocketOne is your whole backend in one file. The `pocketone` executable is a database, a REST and realtime API, user
accounts and sign-in, file storage, an admin dashboard, a server for your pages and static files, and a JavaScript
runtime for your own code, plus PocketOne's extensions (deploys, restore, API tokens, AI models, MCP). There's nothing
else to install and nothing else to run.

An app is a folder. You start `pocketone` in it, and everything it keeps sits next to it.

## Start it

```bash
mkdir myapp && cd myapp
pocketone superuser upsert admin@example.com 'a long password' --dir ./pb_data
pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data
```

```
Server started at http://127.0.0.1:8090
> Dashboard: http://127.0.0.1:8090/_/
> REST API:  http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/
```

- **`--dir`** is the app's data folder. Without it, `pocketone` uses `pb_data` next to the executable, so pass it (or
  set `dir:` in the [configuration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/pocketone-yaml)'s `app:` section) to keep each app's data in its own folder.
- **`--http`** is where it listens (default `127.0.0.1:8090`); `--http 0.0.0.0:8090` listens on every address.
  `pocketone serve example.com` serves HTTPS for that domain, with a certificate it gets and renews itself.
- **`--dev`** prints every request and SQL statement, catches outgoing mail when no mail server is set (and shows it
  at http://127.0.0.1:8025), and skips a hook file with an error instead of stopping.
- Stop it with Ctrl-C. Nothing else is running: no database server, no queue, no worker.

`pocketone --help` lists every command; `pocketone serve --help` every flag. To keep it running on a server, see
[Run on a Linux server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/guides/linux-server).

## What's in the folder

| Folder | What it holds | Backed up | Deployed and synced | Safe to delete |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pb_data` | the database, uploaded files, logs | yes | never | no: it's your data |
| `pb_hooks` | your server code: [hooks](https://pocketone.dev/docs/hooks) and [routes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/routes) (`*.pb.ts`), and `*.pb.wasm` modules | as code, in git | yes | no |
| `pb_pages` | your site's [pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages) | as code, in git | yes | no |
| `pb_migrations` | your [migrations](https://pocketone.dev/docs/migrations): collection changes and seed data | as code, in git | yes | no |
| `pb_public` | static files served as they are (a built single-page app, images) | as code, in git | yes | no |
| `pb_templates` | page templates you ejected (`pocketone template eject`) | as code, in git | yes | no |
| `pb_cache` | files extensions can rebuild, one folder each | never | never | yes, at any time |

Only `pb_data` is created for you; make the others when you need them. The app also writes `types.d.ts` and a
`tsconfig.json` next to them, so your editor knows the JavaScript API, and reads `pocketone.yaml` and `.env` from the
same folder if you add them ([Configuration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/pocketone-yaml)). Add `pb_data/` and `pb_cache/` to your
`.gitignore`.

### `pb_data`

| In it | Is |
|---|---|
| `data.db` | the database: every collection and record, the settings |
| `auxiliary.db` | the logs |
| `storage/` | uploaded files, by collection and record (unless files are stored in S3) |
| `backups/` | backups you made (unless they're sent to S3) |
| `litestream/` | the change history for [point-in-time restore](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/restore) |

Never edit these by hand while the app runs, and never open the live database with another tool. Use the dashboard,
the API or your code.

### `pb_cache`

Each extension that keeps disposable files has its own folder, `pb_cache/<extension>/`. Everything in it can be
rebuilt, so deleting it is always safe: the app carries on, perhaps a little slower until the cache fills again.

```bash
pocketone cache                # each extension's folder, its file count and size
pocketone cache clear          # empty every folder
pocketone cache clear <name>   # empty one extension's folder
```

On a multisite host, each instance's `pb_cache` is kept by the host outside the instance's folder, so copies and moves
of an instance never carry it.

## The dashboard and superusers

The dashboard at `/_/` is where you manage the app: collections and records, settings, logs, backups, and the
screens extensions add (AI models, search, tokens, bulk mail).

![Settings in the dashboard: application, mail, files storage, backups, crons, LLM, SQL console and API tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/screenshots/dashboard-settings.jpg)

**Superusers** are the people who can open it. They're records of a built-in collection, `_superusers`, and they can do
everything: see and change every record, past every [API rule](https://pocketone.dev/docs/api-rules), and call the admin endpoints. Keep
them few.

```bash
pocketone superuser upsert admin@example.com 'a long password' --dir ./pb_data   # create, or reset the password
pocketone superuser delete admin@example.com --dir ./pb_data
pocketone superuser otp admin@example.com --dir ./pb_data                       # a one-time password to sign in with
```

Create the first one before the first `serve`. Without any superuser, the app prints a link (and opens it in a
browser, on your own machine) to a page that creates one.

![The dashboard's superuser sign-in](https://pocketone.dev/docs/screenshots/dashboard-superuser-login.jpg)

![The _superusers collection, under System with the tables extensions keep](https://pocketone.dev/docs/screenshots/dashboard-superusers.jpg)

## Your app's users

Your app's own accounts are a different thing: records of an **auth collection** you control. Every app starts with
one, `users`, and you can add more (`customers`, `staff`). Users sign in through the [API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/authentication)
or your [pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/authentication), never the dashboard, and what each may do is decided by your
collections' [API rules](https://pocketone.dev/docs/api-rules).

![The users collection: your app's accounts, with email, verified and name](https://pocketone.dev/docs/screenshots/dashboard-users.jpg)

| | Superusers | Users |
|---|---|---|
| Collection | `_superusers` (built in) | `users`, or any auth collection you add |
| Sign in at | the dashboard (`/_/`), the CLI, the admin API | your app: the [REST API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/authentication), the SDK, your pages |
| May do | everything | what your API rules allow |
| Made by | `pocketone superuser upsert`, or another superuser | signing up, or you, in the dashboard or code |

See [Authentication](https://pocketone.dev/docs/authentication) for sign-in methods, and [API tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/tokens) for scripts
and other apps that call yours.

## Where a request goes

| Path | Served by |
|---|---|
| `/_/` | the dashboard |
| `/api/...` | the [REST API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest): records, auth, files, realtime, and your [custom routes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/routes) |
| `/api/_c/...` | the [extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis) |
| `/mcp` | [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/mcp), for AI agents |
| anything else | your [pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages) in `pb_pages` and the files in `pb_public` |

[Hooks](https://pocketone.dev/docs/hooks) run on all of it: before and after records are saved, on requests, when mail goes out.

## Extension tables

Extensions that store records keep them in collections named `_<extension>_<table>` (`_bulkmail_campaigns`,
`_llm_calls`), so you can tell them from your own at a glance and see which extension owns each. They live in
`pb_data` with the rest of your data, so they're backed up with it. Extensions create and update them with their own
migrations, recorded apart from yours, so `pocketone migrate` never touches them:

```bash
pocketone extensions migrations              # every extension's migrations and when each was applied
pocketone extensions migrate down bulkmail   # revert bulkmail's last migration (its data goes with it)
```
